purpose: When each DNS implementation could first publish or validate an observable, so that onset (RFC -> first zone) can be split into the part spent waiting for code and the part spent waiting for operators.

method.release_dates: git tag -> date of the commit the tag points at. The tag object's own date is useless here: every tag imported from CVS/SVN carries the migration day, which puts BIND 9.0.1 in 2012.
method.attribution: Find the introducing commit by message, then take the earliest-dated stable release tag that contains it. Section-parsing a changelog gets this wrong on projects with long-lived parallel branches: BIND keeps one CHANGES file per branch, so a 2012 entry sits under whatever marker its branch has.
method.guard: A release dated before the commit cannot have shipped it and is discarded.
method.verified: Every row whose claim is a *default* was checked against the commit's file list, because a changed test fixture reads identically in a log. One candidate was dropped on that check -- see notes.

notes: A candidate row was dropped: BIND commit ca391cd0 (2018-12-05) reads 'Change the default algorithm to RSASHA256 and the alternative algorithm to RSASHA1'. Its file list is bin/tests/system/conf.sh.in and conf.sh.win32 only -- the system-test fixture, not the product. BIND's shipped default is not claimed here.

Capability is recorded, not conflated: 'rrtype' (can parse/serve the type), 'publish' (can generate it), 'sign' (can produce RRSIGs with it), 'validate' (can verify it). BIND had CDS record types in 2014 and CDS generation in 2020.

Registry and registrar platforms are out of scope and are not open source. Where a spike is attributed to an operator below, the attribution is to the operator, never to a particular piece of software they might run.

standard_codepoint=false marks an implementation shipped on a private or provisional codepoint. Those rows are evidence that the cryptography was ready, but they are excluded from code-lag arithmetic: nothing published under codepoint 250 is an RFC 8080 observation.

confidence was removed. It was an unexplained three-level label. Each row now carries attribution (exact / earliest-of-several / approximate) plus attribution_basis saying in words what is uncertain, and evidence_url pointing at the commit so the claim can be checked rather than trusted.

RFC 5011 rows for BIND 9.7.0 added 2026-09-15: managed-keys (validator) and dnssec-revoke (signer). The revoked-KSK series in the forward corpus starts in its first month (2016-06), so with BIND able to revoke from 2010-02 the first-seen date is left-censored.
